ui.outdated: This translation may be out of date: the English page is newer.

refs.event.intro: The viewer adds an **Event type** column to every dataset that has an event column (`event`, `events`, `event_type` or `event_name`). Each game's own words are mapped to one of these kinds (upper and lower case alike); a word not listed counts as *Other*.
refs.event.classes.intro: The **Vehicle class** and **Target class** columns use these classes, worked out from vehicle names (through the [figure catalogue](figures.md)) and type columns.
refs.columns.intro: When a file is loaded, each role is given to the first column whose name matches one of these patterns (regular expressions, tried in order; `i` = any case). Every guess can be changed in [Column mapping](column-mapping.md), and a Parquet file can name its columns itself ([the `heat3d` hints](data-formats.md#the-heat3d-hints)).
refs.languages.intro: The viewer speaks {n} languages. It starts in the browser's language when it has it, and the language menu at the top of the sidebar changes it. How to change it, and how translations are made: [Languages](languages.md).
refs.keys.intro: So that a loaded session is not lost to a stray shortcut, the viewer keeps these keys from the browser.
refs.keys.ctrl.effect: the browser's action (print, save, open, reload, new window, close ...) does not happen
refs.keys.plain.effect: the browser's action (help, find, reload, address bar, caret browsing) does not happen
refs.keys.locked.effect: locked for the viewer (Keyboard Lock API), so the browser does not act on them
refs.keys.close.when: with data or a level loaded
refs.keys.outro: All the viewer's own keys: [Keyboard and mouse reference](keyboard-reference.md).
refs.settings.intro: What the viewer keeps in your browser (`localStorage`) between visits. Nothing of it is sent anywhere. Clearing the site data in the browser removes it all.
refs.settings.outro: Heat settings, filters and the view mode are not kept: they start fresh with each load.
refs.settings.m.heat3d.units: the units preset and single units
refs.settings.m.heat3d.far: figures at a distance, symbols, hit marks, aim lines
refs.settings.m.heat3d.replay: replay labels, tactical display, 2D map, charts, head-up display, look, buildings, follow camera
refs.settings.m.heat3d.inspect: the pick card and camera readout
refs.settings.m.heat3d.carNames: car names in the race tab
refs.settings.m.heat3d.ai: external AI: provider, address, model, options (not the key)
refs.settings.m.heat3d.ai.key: the external AI key, only when *Remember the key* is ticked
refs.values.intro: The price tables of [Value weighting](value-weighting.md). The game is recognised from names in the data; a converter's own value columns in the game's currency win over these.
refs.tools.intro: The command-line tools in the viewer's `tools/` folder (Node.js, run from the repository root). You never need them to use the viewer: they pack, summarise and convert your data, and help whoever maintains the viewer. Each entry has the first paragraph of the tool's own description and its usage lines; run a tool without arguments for its full help where it has one. The data tools of the [related repositories](index.md#related-repositories) document their own commands.
refs.tools.dev.intro: These check the viewer, make the demo data and the screenshots, and write the reference pages.
refs.tools.lib.item: `{tool}` is a library with no command line: the tools above import it to read and write the [.3dheat file](container.md).
